title: Immuta Data Policies
subtitle: Subscription, masking, and row rules by tag
content:
🎫 Two Policy Kinds, Three Scopes (Verified vs 2026.1 Docs)

  • Subscription policies = table access (who may subscribe). Data policies = inside the table (row filters, column/cell masking).
  • Scopes: local (one table) → domain (domain's tables) → global (by tag across the estate — write once, e.g. mask tag PII everywhere).
  • Merge logic (no shortcuts — see table below): row/data policies AND together (OR only inside one policy). Subscription ABAC merge is per-policy: Always Required = AND, Share Responsibility = OR. Non-ABAC subscription conflicts (Anyone / Anyone-who-asks / Individual users) resolve by descending policy-name order with owner override — renaming a policy can flip enforcement. Guardrails, where they apply, are always required on top of any grant.
Policy kindCombineExample
Row / data policiesAND (all apply)Two row filters both filter; OR needs one policy with OR inside
Subscription ABAC, Always RequiredANDMust satisfy this grant AND any other applicable grant
Subscription ABAC, Share ResponsibilityORAny one Share Responsibility grant suffices (guardrails still AND on top)
Non-ABAC subscription conflictDescending name order + owner overrideRenaming Zebra→Alpha can flip the winner — treat renames as policy changes
GuardrailsAlways AND on topTraining-complete required even with manager approval (see quiz q4)

Staging procedure (do not edit globals live): 1) draft in a dev project on sampled tables → 2) staged=true dry-run, verify Pending→Enforced and row counts on a canary table → 3) run the lockout test (mis-scoped table must return zero rows) → 4) promote with staged=false plus rollback note (previous tag mapping + policy export).

Immuta global masking: tag-targeted, auditor exception 
# SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE — field names simplified; verify against the
# Immuta 2026.1 v2 policy API / builder before pasting anywhere.
# Last verified (semantics): 2026-09 vs Immuta policy API + data-policy docs.
name: Finance PII masking
policyKey: data masking pii       # global data policy, applies by tag
type: data
actions:
  type: mask
  maskType: hash                  # intelligent fallback: numerics -> NULL
  exceptions:                     # exclusionary condition
    groups: [AUDIT]               # everyone masked EXCEPT auditors
circumstances:                    # tag targeting lives HERE, not in actions
  - type: columnTags               # NOT literal column names: tags survive renames
    columnTag: PII
staged: false
# SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE — field names simplified; verify against the # Immuta 2026.1 v2 policy API / builder before pasting anywhere. # Last verified (semantics): 2026-09 vs Immuta policy API + data-policy docs. name: Finance PII masking policyKey: data masking pii # global data policy, applies by tag type: data actions: type: mask maskType: hash # intelligent fallback: numerics -> NULL exceptions: # exclusionary condition groups: [AUDIT] # everyone masked EXCEPT auditors circumstances: # tag targeting lives HERE, not in actions - type: columnTags # NOT literal column names: tags survive renames columnTag: PII staged: false

🧠 Advanced DSL: Attributes Meeting Tags

The reviewed Advanced-DSL pattern subscribes users whose attribute matches a tag on the data source — ABAC without per-table rules:

Immuta Advanced DSL: attribute-equals-tag subscription 
# Spelling confirmed 2026-09 vs Immuta Advanced-DSL guide
# (advanced-dsl-policies: "@hasTagsAsAttribute('Department', 'dataSource')").
# SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE around it — build in the UI/API and diff the export.
# Performance note from the docs: thousands of @table-permutation rules
# slow resolution — prefer tag/attribute patterns like this one.
name: Department auto-subscribe
policyKey: subscription entitlements advanced boolean
type: subscription
actions:
  type: entitlements
  advanced: "@hasTagsAsAttribute('Department', 'dataSource')"
  # Department.Marketing users auto-subscribe to Marketing-tagged sources
  automaticSubscription: true   # trade-off: thousands of auto-subscribed
  allowDiscovery: false         # tables is a UX/cost decision, not free
# Spelling confirmed 2026-09 vs Immuta Advanced-DSL guide # (advanced-dsl-policies: "@hasTagsAsAttribute('Department', 'dataSource')"). # SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE around it — build in the UI/API and diff the export. # Performance note from the docs: thousands of @table-permutation rules # slow resolution — prefer tag/attribute patterns like this one. name: Department auto-subscribe policyKey: subscription entitlements advanced boolean type: subscription actions: type: entitlements advanced: "@hasTagsAsAttribute('Department', 'dataSource')" # Department.Marketing users auto-subscribe to Marketing-tagged sources automaticSubscription: true # trade-off: thousands of auto-subscribed allowDiscovery: false # tables is a UX/cost decision, not free

🔍 Critical Review Notes (Straight From the Docs)

  • Intelligent fallbacks: hashing a numeric column would corrupt its type — Immuta falls back to NULL automatically. Never hand-roll hash-on-numeric.
  • Lockout policy: a global row-filter referencing a column a table lacks (use @columnTagged, not hard-coded names) blocks ALL rows rather than leaking. Fail-closed at the data plane.
  • Deeper tag wins — with a tie-break: PII.SSN policy beats PII policy on the same column; at the same depth the earliest-authored policy wins — never rely on creation order, consolidate the policies instead.
  • Row filters AND together: two row policies both apply; to OR them, build one policy with an OR.

🔒 Lock-in / Bill / Exit (Read Before You Commit)

  • Lock-in (documented): SaaS control plane holds your tag taxonomy, policy definitions, and audit history; enforcement is per-compute integration (Snowflake/Databricks/etc.). Your governance metadata gravity wells here.
  • Bill (estimate — confirm current pricing): platform subscription plus per-compute/enforcement footprint; thousands of auto-subscribed tables and @table-permutation rules also cost resolution time and UX noise (see DSL note above).
  • Exit (documented pattern): tag taxonomy ports as column/table labels; masking/row logic rewrites to native Snowflake masking + row-access policies or Databricks Unity Catalog views/RLS. Budget a rewrite — there is no policy export that executes elsewhere.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Switch viewer roles and watch PII masking vs auditor exception vs owner bypass. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What is the difference between subscription and data policies?

options.text: Subscription = table access; data = rows/columns/cells inside subscribed tables
Subscription is for databases, data is for email

questions.explanation: Docs-verified split: subscription gates the table; data policies shape what subscribed users see inside it.

questions.question: Two global subscription grants (one Always Required, one Share Responsibility) and one guardrail apply. An admin renames the Share Responsibility policy from 'Zebra' to 'Alpha'. What must you check? (see merge truth table above)

options.text: Whether non-ABAC conflicts now resolve differently — name order decides them, and the Always Required grant still ANDs with everything
Only whether the guardrail still exists
Nobody — policies conflict so nobody gets in

questions.explanation: Real merge rules: subscription ABAC merge is per-policy (Always Required=AND, Share Responsibility=OR); non-ABAC conflicts resolve by descending name order with owner override — so renames CAN flip enforcement. Guardrails stay mandatory on top.

questions.question: A hash-masking policy hits a numeric salary column. What happens?

options.text: Intelligent fallback to NULL (hash would corrupt the numeric type)
The column is hashed into a string, breaking the schema
The policy is silently skipped, exposing raw salaries

questions.explanation: Docs-verified fallback preserves type safety AND privacy level. Hand-rolled masking gets this wrong.

questions.question: A global row-filter references a column that one table lacks. Result on that table?

options.text: Lockout: zero rows returned until the policy is fixed (fail-closed, no leak)

questions.explanation: Lockout trades availability for confidentiality on mis-scoped globals — and is why @columnTagged beats hard-coded column names.

questions.question: What does @hasTagsAsAttribute('Department', 'dataSource') achieve?

options.text: Auto-subscribes users whose Department attribute matches the source's tag — ABAC without per-table rules

questions.explanation: The reviewed Advanced-DSL pattern: attribute-meets-tag scales onboarding to zero-touch per-table work.

questions.question: A user is subscribed to a table but sees zero rows. Which layer is responsible?

options.text: Data policy (row filter or lockout) — subscription gates the table, data policies shape rows

questions.explanation: Empty tables with valid subscriptions are data-policy behavior. Debug rows at the data layer, access at the subscription layer.

questions.question: Attribute Office values drift from tag values (NYC vs New York). Consequence?

options.text: Silent unsubscribes — attribute and tag vocabularies need joint governance

questions.explanation: Attribute-meets-tag only works when both sides spell values identically. Vocabulary drift is silent access loss.

questions.question: A staged global policy shows Pending for an hour. Meaning?

options.text: Still propagating to remote platforms — verify enforcement before announcing anything

questions.explanation: Policy push is eventually consistent across computes. Pending is a state to monitor, not an outcome to assume.
